Biallelic DBH variants abolish dopamine beta-hydroxylase protein or activity. DBH enzyme activity is absent or severely reduced in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid of every patient tested. In transfected cells the common splice-donor allele produces no detectable protein, and the missense alleles tested produce protein that is trapped in the endoplasmic reticulum instead of reaching secretory vesicles.

nodes.description: L-threo-3,4-dihydroxyphenylserine (L-DOPS) is decarboxylated by aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase directly to noradrenaline, bypassing DBH. It is taken up by sympathetic neurons and released on nerve stimulation, restoring sympathetic control. Doses of 400 to 1800 mg/day in 2 to 3 doses (rarely more than 1200 mg) give an almost immediate and sustained response; in children 2 mg/kg/day is titrated towards 5 to 10 mg/kg/day. The last dose is taken well before bedtime. Plasma noradrenaline rises but seldom normalises, adrenaline mostly stays undetectable, and orthostatic hypotension usually persists in milder form. Continuing it in pregnancy appears safe on limited data.

nodes.description: Baroreflex afferents and sympathetic efferent firing are intact, but the efferent signal has no vasoconstrictor transmitter, so blood pressure falls profoundly on standing. Supine blood pressure is normal or low, with no supine hypertension, and the normal nocturnal dip is absent. Supine exercise is better tolerated than in degenerative autonomic failure, possibly because dopamine and co-transmitters are still released.

nodes.description: Sympathetic postganglionic neurons are present and fire normally, and their central reflex control is intact, but they release no noradrenaline. Cholinergic sympathetic (sweating) and parasympathetic functions are preserved.
